selected_evidence.requirement: Daily rotation configured with 7 compressed rotations retained, and app can continue writing after rotation
selected_evidence.summary: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory (daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate); config validated by logrotate -d; forced rotation produced app.log.1.gz and truncated app.log while keeping the same inode (256035); subsequent writes to app.log succeeded, proving the app can continue writing post-rotation without restart/signal.

selected_evidence.requirement: Rotation is wired into the system's scheduling mechanism (daily)
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed /etc/cron.daily/logrotate (standard Ubuntu 16.04 mechanism) invokes /usr/sbin/logrotate /etc/logrotate.conf, which includes /etc/logrotate.d/*, and the logrotate status file already tracks last rotation time for this log.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (f41e1f8a-dd2a-4b61-aa04-d64b0923b603) plus healthy logrotate config, rotated data, and dry-run validation before restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sudo shutdown -r now' returned an immediate acknowledgement (connection drop confirms the reboot command was accepted and executed).

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: changed boot identity proving actual restart
selected_evidence.summary: Node1 was unreachable immediately after reboot (connection refused), then came back with boot_id 8f51a526-4707-4fa0-a321-856f3558b314, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a genuine kernel restart occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: post-restart recovery of required config/data
selected_evidence.summary: After restart, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory config, app.log content, app.log.1.gz rotated archive, logrotate dry-run validation, and /etc/cron.daily/logrotate hook were all confirmed intact and functional.

#!/bin/sh

# Clean non existent log file entries from status file
cd /var/lib/logrotate
test -e status || touch status
head -1 status > status.clean
sed 's/"//g' status | while read logfile date
do
    [ -e "$logfile" ] && echo "\"$logfile\" $date"
done >> status.clean
mv status.clean status

test -x /usr/sbin/logrotate || exit 0
/usr/sbin/logrotate /etc/logrotate.conf
